title: A read-only black-start core over a copied body home (acceptance H.G13)
problem: tests/recovery/recovery-tests.yaml declares black_start_environment (primary unavailable: a read-only core reads ledger and constitution, asserts shutdown, revokes credentials, notifies Alfonso; workflows/shutdown-recovery.yaml stage 1), and the harness reported it NOT RUN because no such core existed.
founder_intent_refs: docs/FOUNDER_EFFECT_COMPILER.md: 'Make UNIIMENTE immortal' compiles to continuity across component failure, recovery and shutdown-safe restoration
baseline: #196 12119590: greg/recovery.py restores a body from its seed (a writer); greg status reads a live home; no command reads a stopped body's copy and reports the stage-1/stage-2 facts without writing.

alternatives.name: Proposed: greg/black_start.py and `greg --home COPY black-start`
alternatives.description: Compose existing readers: EvidenceLedger(read_only, tail=ignore).verify_chain, compile_constitution, the heartbeat published-head rule, body.booted/body.stopped, device_delegations, compute.node_states/unrevoked_nodes, founder_keys. Output the revocations as unsigned founder commands and the notification as a file outside the home.
advantages: No new state, no key, no write in the home
Every fact comes from an existing reader the body itself uses
The listed commands are the real command kinds, so the founder's signature is the only missing step
disadvantages: A second reader of shutdown facts beside greg status
Reads the whole ledger into memory
Shown-down judged from the copy only: a body still running elsewhere cannot be seen

alternatives.name: Extend greg status with a --black-start flag
disadvantages: status is the live founder projection; mixing the copy-only escalate rule into it couples two contracts
alternatives.revival_evidence: status grows a copy-mode for other reasons

alternatives.name: Sign the revocations in the core
alternatives.description: Give the core the founder key so it revokes directly.
disadvantages: A recovery tool holding the founder key widens authority; intelligence never creates authority

alternatives.name: Send the notification
alternatives.description: Email or push from the core.
disadvantages: Needs a founder-authorized outbound channel; outside contact is founder-only

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: black_start_environment stays NOT RUN; a founder with only a copied home has no tool that tells him whether it verifies, whether the body was down, and what to revoke.
disadvantages: Recovery stage 1 has no executable path

roles.position: Preserves the continuity destination with the strongest real mechanism: verify, report, propose; the founder signs.
material_concerns: Must not imply a notification was sent

roles.position: Composition of existing readers in a new module; greg/recovery.py (six open PRs) and greg/body.py untouched beyond imports.
material_concerns: Drift between this shutdown rule and status's

roles.position: Attacked with a tampered head, a rollback, another constitution, a live copy and a notification path inside the home; each refused or escalated, nothing derived from unverified history.
material_concerns: A rollback within the heartbeat's one-turn window is not detected (same limit as the boot guard)

roles.position: One command with exit codes 0/1/3 an operator can script; it works with no access to the original machine.
material_concerns: Must be run on a copy; on a live home it reports not shown down and still writes nothing

roles.position: The report lists credential identifiers and labels only; no secret leaves the home; the notification file is 0600 and never overwrites.
material_concerns: The report includes device labels the founder chose

evidence.claim: Over a stopped body's copy the core verifies, shows down, lists the phone and node revocations and writes the NOT_SENT notification; the copy is byte-identical afterwards
evidence.finding: passed; original home deleted before the run

evidence.claim: The listed revocations are the real commands
evidence.finding: founder-signed into another copy, the body applies them; a second core run lists nothing to revoke
tampered head, rollback by three records, another constitution: exit 3, credentials and shutdown null, copy unwritten

evidence.claim: The tests catch the checks they rely on
evidence.finding: published-head check removed: caught; shown_down forced true: caught; constitution comparison removed: survived the integration test, then caught by the added unit test

counterevidence.claim: The integration test alone covered every check
counterevidence.finding: it did not: the other-constitution damage fails on the genesis record, not on the comparison; a unit test now isolates the comparison

counterevidence.claim: A signed BODY_STOP leaves a copy the body would resume
counterevidence.finding: the stop persists as a STOP file; resuming a copy needs `greg start --local` (local physical authority), which the test runs and the report shows

pass_1.intended_outcome: With only a copy of a stopped body's home, the founder learns whether its history verifies, whether it was down, and exactly what to sign to end every standing credential, and nothing in the copy changes.

advantages.statement: Stage 1 of the shutdown-recovery workflow has an executable path
advantages.amplified_value: The harness now runs all four declared recovery scenarios; none is reported NOT RUN

advantages.statement: Revocations are emitted as the exact command bodies
advantages.amplified_value: A future authorized channel can carry them to the founder's signer unchanged

disadvantages.statement: Second reader of shutdown facts beside greg status
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Both read the same records (body.booted main_loop, body.stopped, heartbeat); the core adds only the copy-mode escalate rule

disadvantages.statement: Shown-down cannot see a body still running on another machine
disadvantages.redesigned_response: The report says what it judged from (last boot, stop record, heartbeat) and a live copy reports not shown down; an external anchor (greg/anchor.py) is the stronger signal
Read-only and offline; same cost as greg status

pass_2.attack_summary: Attack the strengthened design: a copy with a valid chain but a rolled-back tail; a config naming another constitution; an output path inside the home or over an existing file; an expired delegation on a copy whose clock is wrong; a live copy.

new_weaknesses.statement: Rollback hidden by a matching heartbeat rewrite
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Out of scope for a copy-only reader, as for the boot guard; anchor witnesses cover it (recorded residual)

new_weaknesses.statement: An expired delegation might be omitted on a trusted-clock assumption
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: device_delegations lists expired keys; the core lists them for revocation (unit test)

new_weaknesses.statement: Notification written into the home or over evidence
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Refused inside the home; O_EXCL refuses overwrite (unit and integration tests)

pass_1_disadvantage_disposition.D2: accepted with owner this workstream; residual recorded in H.G13 closed_by

dissent.handling: No dissent recorded. Self-review by one session in five lenses, not independent review.

steps: Revert the commit; black_start_environment returns to NOT RUN and H.G13 to OPEN

kill_criteria: The core writes anything inside an assessed home
It derives credentials or shutdown state from history that does not verify
It reports a live body as shown down
review_trigger: The first black-start run on a real founder body, or a founder-authorized notification channel
